profile.title: Ph.D. Candidate in Chemical Engineering
profile.tagline: Electrocatalysis · Atomically Dispersed Sites · Oxygen Reduction Reaction
profile.bio: I am a Ph.D. candidate in Chemical Engineering at Tsinghua University. My research focuses on non-precious metal catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), bridging experimental synthesis and characterization with density-functional theory to uncover structure–activity relationships at atomically dispersed active sites in surface catalytic processes.
profile.address: Room 310, Yingshi Building, Haidian District, Beijing

publications.title: Efficient harvesting of electricity, aromatic aldehydes and H₂ from lignin over nanoflower-like cobalt-based bifunctional electrocatalysts
publications.highlight: Self-powered electrocatalytic system using nanoflower-like Co-catalysts for integrated lignin valorization. High-current electrodeposition on Ni foam yields a bifunctional catalyst that simultaneously harvests electricity (196.1 mW cm⁻² peak), aromatic aldehydes (2.90–3.34% yield) and H₂ (12.7 mL cm⁻²) from lignin.

publications.title: Internally hollow Cu₂O nanoframes with the abundance of {110} facets enhance direct propylene epoxidation
publications.highlight: Engineered Cu₂O nanoframes via ligand-protected facet etching achieve 0.18 mmol g_cat⁻¹ h⁻¹ PO formation rate with 83.8% selectivity at 175 °C. DFT and characterization confirm Cu₂O {110} facets promote active oxygen species generation and selective epoxidation.

publications.title: Circumventing radical generation on Fe-V atomic pair catalyst for robust oxygen reduction and zinc-air batteries
publications.highlight: ORR pathway-switching strategy on DFT-guided Fe₁V₁-NC atomic pair catalysts circumvents ROS generation. The N₂–Fe–N₂–V–N₂ configuration enables direct O=O bond cleavage (side-on adsorption), achieving 16 mV decay over 50 k cycles, E₁/₂ = 0.89 V, and 400 h zinc-air battery durability at 10 mA cm⁻².

publications.title: Low-coordinate Cu₁–N₂ sites in single-atom catalyst for highly efficient propylene epoxidation with molecular oxygen
publications.highlight: A novel Cu₁–N₂ single-atom catalyst for direct propylene epoxidation, with record PO formation rates. Characterization and DFT show exclusive Cu–N coordination enhances electrophilic oxygen species formation, enabling selective C=C bond activation.

Comfortable bridging experimental and theoretical work, communicating effectively with experimental collaborators.
Programming in Python, MATLAB and C; team player with strong execution under deadlines.
